Some musings on Hubski: You'll see some border-line SJW stuff on there, but people are generally rational and open to debate/differing viewpoints.

It also has virtually no central moderation (excepting severe cases), but people are free to mute others from commenting on their posts. Most of the people are really conservative with the mute button though, so as long as you aren't invasive and abrasive you usually won't get muted, and even then people are mostly happy to ignore you and let you engage with other people on their threads. I actually love their self-moderation style because of the environment it creates.

The site is centered around discussion and debate rather than easy to digest content, so don't expect a ton of posts, but what is there is really good if you're open-minded. All in all an excellent alternative to Reddit if you want this kind of stuff.

Source: I was a member under another username once upon a time. Probably will return now to see if I can get away from Reddit almost completely.

The only place where I disagree with the author is his opinion that Imperator-class Star Destroyers are capital ships, akin to a battlecruiser or a battleship.

From Curtis Saxon's page:

According to the reports of Rebel Alliance historian Arhul Hextrophon (in The Imperial Sourcebook) the Galactic Empire has a about three to five dozen or so destroyers in an average sector group fleet, of which there is at least one for each of the Empire's thousands of sectors. This indicates that the local territorial fleets alone account for tens of thousands of star destroyers galaxy-wide. It should be noted that though Hextrophon's reports have proven to be error-prone on many occasions; they consistently tend towards gross underestimates of Imperial naval and military strengths. The true number of star destroyers is probably much greater than the values he implies.

This is supported in the films. For the first movie, you have a single destroyer fulfilling a role not fit for a capital ship - hunting for a lead for stolen data, hunting down a small corvette, and dispatching scout parties to a remote world. In the second movie, you have a group of destroyers escorting an actual capital ship, and in the third movie it is illustrated that the Executor was not really unique ("Relax kid, there are a lot of command ships"). In addition, there is a second large Imperial ship present at the Battle of Endor (again, see Curtis Saxon's page for screenshots)
This is a high-quality page. I am glad that I got to read it.
